research_question: Does instructor beauty affect teaching productivity as reflected in student instructional ratings?

ivs.description: rating of the instructor's physical appearance by a panel of six students, averaged across the six panelists and shifted to have a mean of zero.

dv.description: course overall teaching evaluation score, on a scale of 1 (very unsatisfactory) to 5 (excellent).

controls.description: number of students that participated in the evaluation.
factor. Does the instructor belong to a minority (non-Caucasian)?
factor. Is the instructor a native English speaker?
factor. Is the instructor on tenure track?
factor. Is the course a single-credit elective (e.g., yoga, aerobics, dance)?
factor. Is the course an upper or lower division course? (Lower division courses are mainly large freshman and sophomore courses).

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Load data
path = "teachingratings.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(path)

# Basic checks
# Drop rows with missing values in relevant columns
cols = [
    "eval",
    "beauty",
    "age",
    "gender",
    "minority",
    "native",
    "tenure",
    "credits",
    "division",
    "students",
]
df = df[cols].dropna()

# Fit OLS with categorical controls
formula = (
    "eval ~ beauty + age + students + C(gender) + C(minority) + C(native) "
    "+ C(tenure) + C(credits) + C(division)"
)
model = smf.ols(formula, data=df).fit(cov_type="HC3")

print("N:", int(model.nobs))
print("Beauty coef:", model.params.get("beauty"))
print("Beauty p-value:", model.pvalues.get("beauty"))
print(model.summary())

# Also compute simple correlation
corr = df[["eval", "beauty"]].corr().iloc[0, 1]
print("Correlation eval-beauty:", corr)
